acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW sustained-overrun semantics: incoming events beyond capacity are refused or counted as dropped while older queued accepted events drain in original order.
DROP_OLD sustained-overrun semantics: oldest queued events are evicted for newer arrivals with deterministic retained-tail ordering.
BLOCK sustained-overrun semantics: producer path waits for consumer drain capacity, releases on capacity, policy swap, or shutdown, preserves all accepted events, and does not busy-spin.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained-overrun semantics: excess events spill through MmapJournal-compatible storage, read back correctly, and drain FIFO after in-memory backlog permits.
Edge-level hot-swap semantics: changing one edge policy affects only that edge, applies atomically to subsequent enqueue decisions, and preserves in-memory queue plus spill invariants.
R-002 snapshot prerequisite coverage: overflow implementation proceeds only when the snapshot prerequisite and MmapJournal-compatible lifecycle boundary are present and documented.
Lifecycle and durability coverage: stale or invalid spill files, CRC-equivalent or invariant failures, and failure or partial-acceptance paths are handled deterministically.
Forbidden-scope coverage: no custom policies, priority shedding, source-specific shedding, or cross-partition backpressure propagation are introduced.
Configured QA gate coverage: ./qa/smoke.sh, ./qa/regression.sh, Gradle module tests, and ./gradlew jmhSmokeCheck pass with allocation gate green.
assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner edge queues are the runtime enforcement point for backpressure behavior.
GraphPartitionRunner.Builder is implemented in runtime-core, with public API types exposed through dag-framework-api where needed.
BackpressurePolicy is a closed enum, not an extension point for custom policy code.
Overflow spill reuses dag-framework-lvc or lvc-standard MmapJournal-compatible machinery rather than introducing a new durable file format.
R-006 is dependency-gated on the R-002 snapshot prerequisite; design must verify the prerequisite from repo-memory/ROADMAP.md and repo-memory/DECISIONS.md before overflow implementation proceeds.
Hot-swap semantics are edge-scoped, affect future enqueue behavior, and do not propagate backpressure across partitions.
Allocation gate coverage is represented by existing smoke, regression, Gradle test, and benchmark smoke checks including jmhSmokeCheck.

acceptance_test_matrix: DROP_NEW sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies incoming overflow is dropped while accepted records remain ordered.
DROP_OLD sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies oldest buffered records are shed and later accepted records drain in expected order.
BLOCK sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies producer blocking, later progress after drain, and no deadlock during shutdown.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK sustained-overrun semantic coverage verifies mmap spill creation, ordered drain, readback correctness, and spill resource retirement.
Edge-level hot-swap coverage verifies policy changes apply atomically without corrupting buffered, dropped, blocked, or spilled records.
Lifecycle/durability coverage verifies stale/invalid spill state, invariant/CRC-equivalent invariant failure, and partial spill acceptance/failure outcomes.
Configured QA gate coverage verifies qa/smoke.sh, qa/regression.sh, gradle test suite, and jmhSmokeCheck remain green.
assumptions: GraphPartitionRunner and its Builder live under runtime-core source ownership, with public API types also exposed through dag-framework-api where needed.
Existing lvc-standard MmapJournal machinery is available under dag-framework-lvc and can be reused for overflow spill persistence.
QA may add failing tests and fixtures before implementation, but implementation slices must not edit registered QA/test roots.

acceptance_tests: Sustained-overrun matrix covers DROP_NEW, DROP_OLD, BLOCK, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK.
DROP_NEW proves excess incoming records are rejected while accepted records remain ordered.
DROP_OLD proves oldest buffered records are shed and newest accepted records drain correctly.
BLOCK proves producers wait for capacity and make progress after consumer drain without deadlock.
OVERFLOW_TO_DISK proves spill file writes, drains, and reads back correctly in order.
Hot-swap test proves an edge can change policy without corrupting buffered or spilled records.
Overflow failure coverage includes stale/invalid spill state, invariant/CRC-equivalent invariant failure, and partial spill acceptance/failure behavior.
jmhSmokeCheck, qa/smoke.sh, and qa/regression.sh pass.
design_contract.concurrency_protocol: Each edge applies its configured policy independently under sustained producer overrun: DROP_NEW rejects incoming records when full, DROP_OLD evicts oldest buffered records before accepting new records, BLOCK waits without busy spinning until capacity/drain is available, and OVERFLOW_TO_DISK spills excess records while preserving drain order. Hot-swap must be atomic at the edge level and must not propagate backpressure across partitions.
forbidden_alternatives: New bespoke spill binary format outside MmapJournal.
Global runner-level policy only with no per-edge config.
Best-effort overflow that does not verify readback/drain ordering.
Priority or QoS-based record shedding.
Blocking implementation that busy-spins or deadlocks runner shutdown/drain.
hard_constraints: Do not add custom backpressure policies.
Do not add priority-based shedding.
Do not add cross-partition backpressure propagation.
Reuse MmapJournal machinery from lvc-standard/dag-framework-lvc instead of inventing a new spill format.
Allocation gate and jmhSmokeCheck must remain green.
qa/smoke.sh and qa/regression.sh must pass.
design_contract.ownership_boundaries: dag-framework-api owns public enum/config surface; runtime-core owns GraphPartitionRunner queue/backpressure behavior and hot-swap semantics; dag-framework-lvc owns reusable MmapJournal-backed overflow persistence integration; QA roots own acceptance tests and fixtures only.
design_contract.persistence_protocol: OVERFLOW_TO_DISK must reuse existing MmapJournal machinery from lvc-standard/dag-framework-lvc for spill files, drain spilled records back in deterministic order, close/delete or otherwise retire spill resources after drain, and treat stale/invalid spill state or invariant failure as testable failure paths rather than silently corrupting data.
